name: Unattended Run: anonymous orkes session, relay the claim link once, exit 9 step-up
query: I'm kicking this off and stepping away for a couple of hours, so don't wait on me for anything. On Orkes, build and run a workflow that takes a lead record, scores it with an LLM, and posts hot leads to our webhook — plus a Python worker for the `enrich_lead` task. Nothing is set up on this machine yet. When I'm back I'd like all of it under my own account.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Treat this as an unattended run on Developer Edition (`https://developer.orkescloud.com`): the user has no server and is not at the keyboard, so start an anonymous session — `orkes login --anonymous` (or `ORKES_ANONYMOUS=1` so `orkes conductor …` starts one itself) — not the device flow (`orkes login --no-wait` would block on a human), not a local `conductor server start`, and not the key + secret / Access Control → Applications flow. Exit 0; begin working immediately.

Step 2: Check `orkes --version` first. If `orkes` is missing, point to its install page; never run a global install without asking. If `orkes login --anonymous` exits 5 with 'anonymous sessions are not enabled on this server's identity provider', fall back to the device flow (`orkes login --no-wait`, relay `Open <url>` / `Code XXXX-XXXX` verbatim) rather than failing.

Step 3: The FIRST time the `Claim it <url>` / `Code XXXX-XXXX` block appears, relay it to the user once, verbatim, in one short sentence ('Your work is in an anonymous session; open <url> whenever you want to keep it under your account, no rush'), then continue. Never block on the claim, never repeat it unprompted, never ask them to paste anything back, never claim to have opened the browser. Never read token/session files, the profiles file, the state dir, the clipboard, or profile YAML.

Step 4: Verify with `orkes identity show` (reports `level 0` / `guest` for an unclaimed session) and `orkes conductor workflow list --json`, reporting names/counts only. Run the Hello World from references/orkes-dev-edition.md BEFORE the lead-scoring goal: write `hello_world.json`, `orkes conductor workflow create hello_world.json`, `orkes conductor workflow start -w hello_world -i '{"who":"World"}' --sync`, and give the execution link.

Step 5: Build the real goal from the closest starter / template (LLM scoring + HTTP webhook + a SIMPLE task) rather than a blank definition. Developer Edition is Enterprise: follow Rule 16 (`integration-list --category AI_MODEL`, integration name as `llmProvider`) and Rule 18 (saved prompt template) before the `LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE` task. Apply Rule 1: `enrich_lead` is a SIMPLE task, so register its task definition and scaffold the Python worker.

Step 6: When `orkes conductor keys create --name <app> --save` exits 9 with 'this action needs a claimed account … Run orkes claim', treat it as a step-up, not an error: stop that action, tell the user that minting worker credentials needs a claimed account, give the claim link again, then either wait with `orkes claim --timeout 60s` a few times (exit 7 = still pending, nothing failed) or continue with the remaining work (worker code, task definition, webhook wiring). Never retry `keys create` blindly, never work around it with pasted keys, and never echo any credential value.

Step 7: If the claim completes (exit 0 — same session, same profile, level 1, the user's email; nothing restarts and the registered workflow already belongs to them), finish `keys create --save` and the worker gate. If it is still pending when the work is done, leave the worker ready to run and state exactly what remains: open the claim link, then `orkes conductor keys create --name <app> --save`. Meanwhile the worker may poll as the guest, inline only (`CONDUCTOR_SERVER_URL="$(orkes profile show --format '{{.conductorUrl}}')" CONDUCTOR_AUTH_TOKEN="$(orkes token)" …`, token ~10 h), never written to chat or a file.

Step 8: Never run `orkes logout` on the unclaimed session — its key on this machine is the only way back to that work (not recoverable by anyone, support included). Commands use `orkes conductor …`; the final report lists the workflow, the execution link, what the worker needs, and that the work stays in the anonymous session until the user claims it.
success_criteria: An anonymous session is started (`orkes login --anonymous`, or `ORKES_ANONYMOUS=1` with `orkes conductor …`) and work begins at once; the device flow is not used as the first step, no local server is started, and the key + secret / browser Applications flow is not the primary path

The `Claim it <url>` line is relayed to the user exactly once, verbatim, in one short sentence that says there is no rush; the agent never blocks waiting for the claim, never asks the user to paste anything back, never claims to have opened the browser, and never reads token/session/profile files

Connectivity is verified with a real `orkes identity show` / `workflow list` call before success is reported, and `level 0` / `guest` is interpreted as an unclaimed anonymous session rather than an error
A Hello World workflow is registered and run (under 30 s, built-in tasks only) BEFORE the lead-scoring build begins

The lead-scoring workflow starts from a named starter/template, uses `LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE` with an Orkes integration name (Rule 16) and a saved prompt template (Rule 18), and `enrich_lead` goes through the worker gate (Rule 1) with a Python worker scaffolded

Exit 9 from `orkes conductor keys create` is treated as a step-up, not a failure: the action stops, the user is told which action needs a claimed account, the claim link is given again, and the agent either polls `orkes claim --timeout 60s` (exit 7 = pending) or continues with other work — it does not retry blindly or ask for keys
No credential value appears in chat, files, or command arguments; `orkes token` is only ever used inline
`orkes logout` is never run on the unclaimed session, and the final report states that the work stays in the anonymous session until the user claims it
